Appendix C: C in one chapter#

Appendices · Appendix C· 7 min read

Every C concept the book teaches, in the groups of the concept index, with one to three sentences each. A concept that a chapter teaches links to that section. A concept kv never needed is taught here, and links to its official reference. Open this appendix six months after the book, when a construct looks familiar and its name has gone.

Types and values#

ConceptWhat to rememberWhere
integer types and stdint.hint, long and friends have platform sizes; int32_t and uint64_t say exactly what they are.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
char signednessPlain char may be signed or unsigned by platform, so a byte over 127 can become negative.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
integer promotion and the usual conversionsSmall types widen to int before arithmetic, so two chars add as ints. When a signed and an unsigned operand meet, the signed one becomes unsigned, and -1 is suddenly the largest value. Compare sizes as size_t and counts as int, and never mix them in one expression.reference
signed overflow is undefinedOverflowing a signed integer is undefined behaviour, so the compiler may assume it never happens.Three answers to the largest integer plus one c/ch05/kv.c
unsigned wrapUnsigned arithmetic wraps around modulo 2^n, by definition, which is how a hash function is allowed to overflow.Three answers to the largest integer plus one c/ch05/kv.c
boolstdbool.h since C99, a keyword in C23. Any non-zero value is true.C17 against C23 c/ch14/extras/c23.c
enumNamed integer constants, with no check that a value is one of the names.switch, and the cases that run into each other c/ch04/kv.c
sizeofThe size of a type or an object in bytes, computed at compile time, with no parentheses needed for an object.What a struct is made of, and an arena c/ch06/generic.c
size_t, ssize_t and ptrdiff_tsize_t is the unsigned type of a size and an index, and sizeof yields it. ssize_t is the signed one that read and write return, so that -1 can mean failure. ptrdiff_t is the type of one pointer minus another.reference
castsAn explicit conversion the compiler will not question, so each one is a claim you must be able to defend.What C does instead of generics c/ch06/generic.c
const and const-correctnessA promise not to write through a pointer, checked by the compiler and carried through every call.The parser stops copying c/ch10/src/resp.h
volatileEvery read and write must happen, because something outside the program can change the value.C: a signal, a flag and a pipe c/ch10/src/stop.h
static, extern and linkagestatic hides a name inside one file; extern says a name is defined elsewhere.C: two files, one binary hello/c/greet.c
translation unitsEach .c file compiles alone, with the headers pasted in, and the linker joins the results.C: two files, one binary hello/c/units.c
storage durationAutomatic variables live until the block ends, static ones for the whole run, allocated ones until free.Where a value lives, and for how long c/ch06/kv.c
stack and heapLocals live on the stack and vanish with the function; malloc gives memory that outlives it.Where a value lives, and for how long c/ch06/kv.c
zero initialisation= {0} sets every member to zero, and a static variable is zero without it.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
designated initialisers{.fd = -1, .len = 0} names the members, so the order of the struct does not matter.C again: poll, kqueue and epoll behind one header c/ch09/src/poller_epoll.c
compound literals(struct pollfd){fd, POLLIN, 0} builds a value in place without a named variable.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c

Pointers and memory#

ConceptWhat to rememberWhere
pointersAn address plus a type, and the type says how many bytes one step is.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
pointer arithmeticp + 1 moves by one element, not one byte, so the type of p decides the step. The result is only defined inside the same object, or one past its end, and the chapter 4 parser stays inside its buffer by comparing against end.reference
arrays decay to pointersAn array name used as a value becomes a pointer to its first element, and the length is gone. That is why a function takes a pointer and a length, and why sizeof an array parameter is the size of a pointer.reference
pointer to pointerHow a function gives its caller a new pointer, as in a grow function that may move a buffer.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
void pointerA pointer to anything, which malloc returns and a callback context uses.What C does instead of generics c/ch06/generic.c
NULL and nullptrThe null pointer. C23 adds nullptr with its own type.C17 against C23 c/ch14/extras/c23.c
malloc, calloc, realloc and freeAsk for bytes, get them zeroed, grow them in place or elsewhere, give them back.Growing, measuring and slicing bytes c/ch05/kv.c
ownership conventionsA comment on every pointer says who frees it, because the compiler will not.The parser stops copying c/ch10/src/resp.h
alignment and offsetofEach type has an alignment, structs get padding to keep it, and offsetof finds a member's position.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/generic.c
flexible array membersA struct whose last member is an array of unknown size, declared as data[], is allocated in one block with room after its header. Redis stores its strings this way, with the length and the bytes in one allocation.reference
restrictA promise that two pointers do not overlap, which lets the compiler optimise.The optimisation levels, measured c/ch13/bench/bench_copy.c
strict aliasingReading an object through a pointer of a different type is undefined, except through char or unsigned char. The compiler may assume an int and a float never overlap, which is why a memcpy is the way to reinterpret bytes.reference
use after free, double free and leaksThe three memory bugs C lets you write, and what each looks like under AddressSanitizer.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted for c/ch06/kv.c
arenasAllocate many small things from one block and free them all at once.What a struct is made of, and an arena c/ch06/generic.c

Basics#

ConceptWhat to rememberWhere
packages and importsA folder is a package, an import is a path, and an unused import is an error.Go: one command, one binary hello/go/main.go
zero valuesEvery variable starts as zero, nil or empty, so a struct is usable without a constructor.Every variable starts at zero hello/go/main.go
:= and varInside a function, := declares and assigns in one step and infers the type. var works anywhere and takes an explicit type or a zero value. A := in an inner scope can declare a new variable that shadows one outside, which is the usual way an err goes missing.reference
const and iotaA const is untyped until it is used, so 1 << 40 is fine where an int would overflow. Inside one const block, iota counts from 0 on each line, which is how the aof package names its three policies.reference
basic types and conversionsint is the machine word, every conversion is written out, and there is no implicit widening.Three answers to the largest integer plus one go/ch05/strings_test.go
runes, strings, bytes and UTF-8A string is immutable bytes, range gives runes, and len counts bytes.Bytes, runes and a builder go/ch05/strings_test.go
arrays against slicesAn array has a fixed length in its type; a slice is a view of one with a length and a capacity.Go: the same table, with nothing to free go/ch06/table.go
len, cap, append and aliasingappend writes into spare capacity, so two slices can share and overwrite the same array.Bytes, runes and a builder go/ch05/exec.go
copy and the full slice expressioncopy duplicates bytes, and s[a:b:c] caps the capacity to stop append from aliasing.The parser stops copying go/ch10/internal/resp/resp.go
mapsReading a nil map is fine and writing one panics; iteration order is random on purpose.Go: two kinds of string, and a copy between them go/ch05/store.go
comma-okv, ok := m[k] separates a missing key from a zero value, and the same form works for assertions and channels.Go: two kinds of string, and a copy between them go/ch05/store.go
structs and composite literalsFields in order or by name, and a pointer to a literal with &.Go: the same table, with nothing to free go/ch06/table.go
pointers against valuesEverything is passed by value, so a function that must change the caller's struct takes a pointer. A method on a pointer receiver can change the value and a method on a value receiver gets a copy. The store's methods all take *Store.reference
the forms of rangeOver a slice, a map, a string, a channel, an integer since 1.22, and a function since 1.23.A function that range can call go/ch08/internal/store/value.go
switch and type switchNo fallthrough by default, cases can be expressions, and switch v := x.(type) branches on a type.Go: any, and a switch on the type go/ch08/internal/store/value.go
labeled break and continueThe way out of a nested loop, with a label on the outer one.A function that range can call

Appendix E: Rust in one chapter#

Appendices · Appendix E· 8 min read

Every Rust concept the book teaches, in the groups of the concept index, with one to three sentences each. A concept that a chapter teaches links to that section. A concept kv never needed is taught here, and links to its official reference. Open this appendix six months after the book, when a construct looks familiar and its name has gone.

Basics#

ConceptWhat to rememberWhere
let, mut and shadowingA binding is immutable unless it says mut, which the compiler enforces. A second let with the same name shadows the first, and may change its type, which is how a parsed value replaces the string it came from.reference
integer overflow rulesDebug builds panic on overflow, release builds wrap, and checked_add and wrapping_add say what you mean.Three answers to the largest integer plus one rust/ch05/src/store.rs
as and From castsas converts between numbers and may truncate or wrap, so n as u8 of 300 is 44. From and Into convert where the conversion cannot fail, and the ? operator uses From to turn one error type into another.reference
tuples, arrays and slicesA tuple groups a fixed set of values of mixed types, and a pattern takes it apart. An array [T; N] has a length in its type. A slice &[T] is a borrowed view of a run of elements, with its length beside the pointer, and it is what every function in kv takes.reference
VecThe growable array that owns its elements and frees them when it drops.Rust: a value has one owner rust/ch05/src/store.rs
String, str, char and bytesString owns valid UTF-8, &str borrows it, char is a code point, and as_bytes gives the bytes.str, String, char and a slice of bytes rust/ch05/src/store.rs
structs and impl blocksData in a struct, behaviour in impl, and a value is built with a literal or a new function.Rust: the table that drops itself rust/ch06/src/table.rs
methods and the forms of self&self reads, &mut self changes, self consumes.Rust: the table that drops itself rust/ch06/src/table.rs
enums with dataEach variant can carry its own fields, which is a sum type the compiler checks.One enum for everything that can go wrong rust/ch04/src/resp.rs
Option and ResultSome or None for a value that may be absent, Ok or Err for one that may fail.Rust: an Option for the end, a Result for the rest rust/ch04/src/resp.rs
match and patternsEvery case must be handled, with guards, bindings, slice and struct patterns, and @.Rust: an Option for the end, a Result for the rest rust/ch04/src/main.rs
if let, let else and while letMatch one pattern without the full match, or leave early when it does not match.Rust: an Option for the end, a Result for the rest rust/ch04/src/resp.rs
loops and labelsloop runs until break, and break may carry a value out of it. while and for are the usual ones, and for takes anything that is an iterator. A label such as 'outer: lets a break or continue name the loop it means.reference
expressions against statementsA block is an expression, and its value is the last line without a semicolon. So if, match and a plain block all produce values, and a function returns the value of its final expression. A semicolon turns an expression into a statement that yields nothing.reference
const and staticA const is inlined, a static has one address, and a mutable static needs unsafe.A table of fn pointers, built by a macro rust/ch05/src/cmd.rs
modules and visibilitymod, pub, pub(crate), use and paths, with files as modules.Rust: a module is a file you must announce rust/ch07/src/store.rs
CargoCrates, features, workspaces, profiles, build.rs and the lockfile, with semantic versioning.Rust: cargo owns the project hello/rust/Cargo.toml
doc comments and doc tests/// becomes documentation, and a code block in it is compiled and run by cargo test.Rust: the compiler already ran, and the tools check the rest rust/ch12/src/resp.rs
rustfmt and clippyThe one formatter and the linter with hundreds of checks, both standard.Rust: cargo owns the project
editionsA crate picks 2015, 2018, 2021 or 2024, and crates of different editions link together.Rust: cargo owns the project hello/rust/Cargo.toml

ConceptWhat to rememberWhere
moveAssigning or passing a value gives it away, and the old name cannot be used again.Rust: a value has one owner rust/ch05/src/cmd.rs
Copy against CloneSmall plain values copy on assignment; everything else moves unless you call clone.A move copies three words rust/ch17/src/lessons.rs
borrows& lends a value for reading, &mut for changing, and the owner waits until the borrow ends.Rust: a value has one owner rust/ch05/src/store.rs
mutable or shared, never bothAny number of readers or one writer at a time, which is the rule that prevents data races.Shared or mutable is a promise about memory rust/ch17/src/main.rs
non-lexical lifetimesA borrow ends at its last use, not at the end of the block.Lifetimes, in the one place kv needs them rust/ch10/src/main.rs

'staticLives for the whole program, as a string literal does, or owns everything it holds.'static is a bound on a type rust/ch17/src/cmd.rs

Drop and RAIIA value is cleaned up when its owner goes out of scope, in reverse order of declaration.Rust: the table that drops itself rust/ch06/src/table.rs

interior mutabilityCell, RefCell and Mutex let you change a value through a shared reference, checked at runtime.Two owners of one table rust/ch06/src/table.rs

BoxOne owner of a value on the heap, which recursive types and trait objects need.Closures and iterators, named at last rust/ch08/src/chain.rs

Appendix F: Concept index#

Every concept the book claims to teach, per language and per group, with the section that teaches it and the kv file that uses it. The build generates this index from the three files under concepts/ and fails when a concept has no section.

C#

Types and values#

ConceptIn one lineTaught inIn kv
integer types and stdint.hint, long and friends have platform sizes; int32_t and uint64_t say exactly what they are.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c
char signednessPlain char may be signed or unsigned by platform, so a byte over 127 can become negative.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c
integer promotion and the usual conversionsSmall types widen to int before arithmetic, so two chars add as ints. When a signed and an unsigned operand meet, the signed one becomes unsigned, and -1 is suddenly the largest value. Compare sizes as size_t and counts as int, and never mix them in one expression.Appendix C
signed overflow is undefinedOverflowing a signed integer is undefined behaviour, so the compiler may assume it never happens.Three answers to the largest integer plus onec/ch05/kv.c

size_t, ssize_t and ptrdiff_tsize_t is the unsigned type of a size and an index, and sizeof yields it. ssize_t is the signed one that read and write return, so that -1 can mean failure. ptrdiff_t is the type of one pointer minus another.Appendix C
castsAn explicit conversion the compiler will not question, so each one is a claim you must be able to defend.What C does instead of genericsc/ch06/generic.c

zero initialisation= {0} sets every member to zero, and a static variable is zero without it.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c

Pointers and memory#

ConceptIn one lineTaught inIn kv
pointersAn address plus a type, and the type says how many bytes one step is.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c
pointer arithmeticp + 1 moves by one element, not one byte, so the type of p decides the step. The result is only defined inside the same object, or one past its end, and the chapter 4 parser stays inside its buffer by comparing against end.Appendix C
arrays decay to pointersAn array name used as a value becomes a pointer to its first element, and the length is gone. That is why a function takes a pointer and a length, and why sizeof an array parameter is the size of a pointer.Appendix C
pointer to pointerHow a function gives its caller a new pointer, as in a grow function that may move a buffer.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c
void pointerA pointer to anything, which malloc returns and a callback context uses.What C does instead of genericsc/ch06/generic.c
NULL and nullptrThe null pointer. C23 adds nullptr with its own type.C17 against C23c/ch14/extras/c23.c
malloc, calloc, realloc and freeAsk for bytes, get them zeroed, grow them in place or elsewhere, give them back.Growing, measuring and slicing bytesc/ch05/kv.c
ownership conventionsA comment on every pointer says who frees it, because the compiler will not.The parser stops copyingc/ch10/src/resp.h
alignment and offsetofEach type has an alignment, structs get padding to keep it, and offsetof finds a member's position.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/generic.c
flexible array membersA struct whose last member is an array of unknown size, declared as data[], is allocated in one block with room after its header. Redis stores its strings this way, with the length and the bytes in one allocation.Appendix C
restrictA promise that two pointers do not overlap, which lets the compiler optimise.The optimisation levels, measuredc/ch13/bench/bench_copy.c
strict aliasingReading an object through a pointer of a different type is undefined, except through char or unsigned char. The compiler may assume an int and a float never overlap, which is why a memcpy is the way to reinterpret bytes.Appendix C
use after free, double free and leaksThe three memory bugs C lets you write, and what each looks like under AddressSanitizer.C: an array of chains, and every pointer accounted forc/ch06/kv.c
arenasAllocate many small things from one block and free them all at once.What a struct is made of, and an arenac/ch06/generic.c

thiserror and anyhowThe two crates most projects use for errors. thiserror derives Display and From for an error enum like the chapter 4 KvError, so that the impl blocks are one attribute each. anyhow is the Box<dyn Error> idea with context, for programs that report errors and never match on them.Appendix E
